# 1 Kings Chapter 14 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** At-that time Abijah son-of Jeroboam became-sick.

**2** And-Jeroboam said to-his-wife, "Arise, please, and-disguise-yourself, and-they-will-not know that you are the-wife-of Jeroboam. And-go to-Shiloh. Behold, there is Ahijah the-prophet — he spoke concerning-me as-king over this people.

**3** And-take in-your-hand ten loaves and-cakes and-a-jar-of honey, and-go to-him. He will-tell you what will-be for-the-boy."

**4** And-the-wife-of Jeroboam did so. And-she-arose and-went to-Shiloh and-came to the-house-of Ahijah. And-Ahijah could-not see, for his-eyes were-set because-of his-old-age.

**5** And-YHWH said to-Ahijah, "Behold, the-wife-of Jeroboam is-coming to-seek a-word from-you concerning her-son, for he is-sick. Thus and-thus you-shall-speak to-her. And-it-shall-be, when-she-comes, she will-be-acting-as-a-stranger."

**6** And-it-was, when-Ahijah heard ʾet-the-sound-of her-feet as-she-came in-the-doorway, and-he-said, "Come-in, wife-of Jeroboam. Why are-you acting-as-a-stranger? And-I am-sent to-you with-a-hard-word.

**7** Go, say to-Jeroboam, 'Thus says YHWH, the-God-of Israel: Because I-exalted-you from-the-midst-of the-people, and-I-made-you prince over my-people Israel,

**8** and-I-tore the-kingdom from the-house-of David and-gave-it to-you — but-you-were not like my-servant David, who kept my-commandments and-who followed-me with-all his-heart, to-do only the-right in-my-eyes,

**9** and-you-did-evil above all who were before-you, and-you-went and-made for-yourself other gods and-molten-images to-provoke-me, and-ʾet-me you-cast behind your-back —

**10** therefore, behold, I am-bringing evil to the-house-of Jeroboam, and-I-will-cut-off from-Jeroboam every male, bond and-free, in-Israel. And-I-will-burn-after the-house-of Jeroboam as-one-burns ʾet-the-dung, until-it-is-finished.

**11** The-one-belonging-to-Jeroboam who-dies in-the-city, the-dogs will-eat. And-the-one-who-dies in-the-field, the-birds-of the-heavens will-eat. For YHWH has-spoken.'

**12** And-you, arise, go to-your-house. When-your-feet enter the-city, the-child will-die.

**13** And-all Israel will-mourn for-him and-bury-him, for this-one alone of-Jeroboam's-house will-come to a-tomb, because there-was-found in-him a-good thing toward YHWH, the-God-of Israel, in-the-house-of Jeroboam.

**14** And-YHWH will-raise-up for-himself a-king over Israel who will-cut-off ʾet-the-house-of Jeroboam — this is the-day! And-what? Even now.

**15** And-YHWH will-strike Israel as-a-reed sways in-the-water, and-he-will-uproot ʾet-Israel from-upon this good land that he-gave to-their-fathers, and-scatter-them beyond the-River, because they-made their-Asherah-poles, provoking YHWH.

**16** And-he-will-give-up ʾet-Israel because-of the-sins-of Jeroboam that he-sinned and-that he-caused-Israel-to-sin."

**17** And-the-wife-of Jeroboam arose and-went and-came to-Tirzah. As-she-came to the-threshold-of the-house, the-boy died.

**18** And-all Israel buried-him and-mourned for-him, according-to-the-word-of YHWH that he-spoke by-the-hand-of his-servant Ahijah the-prophet.

**19** And-the-rest-of the-acts-of Jeroboam, how he-fought and-how he-reigned — behold, they are written in-the-Book-of the-Chronicles-of the-Kings-of Israel.

**20** And-the-days that Jeroboam reigned were twenty-two years. And-he-lay-down with his-fathers, and-Nadab his-son reigned in-his-place.

**21** And-Rehoboam son-of Solomon reigned in-Judah. Forty-one years old was Rehoboam when-he-became-king, and-seventeen years he-reigned in-Jerusalem — the-city that YHWH chose from-all the-tribes-of Israel to-put his-name there. And-the-name-of his-mother was Naamah the-Ammonite.

**22** And-Judah did the-evil in-the-eyes-of YHWH, and-they-provoked-him to-jealousy above all that their-fathers had-done, with-their-sins that they-sinned.

**23** And-they also built for-themselves high-places and-pillars and-Asherah-poles, on every high hill and-under every green tree.

**24** And-also cult-prostitutes were in-the-land. They-did according-to-all the-abominations-of the-nations that YHWH dispossessed from-before the-sons-of Israel.

**25** And-it-was in-the-fifth year-of the-king Rehoboam, Shishak king-of Egypt came-up against Jerusalem.

**26** And-he-took ʾet-the-treasures-of the-house-of YHWH and-ʾet-the-treasures-of the-house-of the-king — ʾet-everything he-took. And-he-took ʾet-all the-shields-of gold that Solomon had-made.

**27** And-the-king Rehoboam made in-their-place shields-of bronze, and-entrusted-them to the-hand-of the-commanders-of the-runners who-guarded the-entrance-of the-house-of the-king.

**28** And-it-was, whenever the-king went to the-house-of YHWH, the-runners would-carry-them, and-they-would-return-them to the-chamber-of the-runners.

**29** And-the-rest-of the-acts-of Rehoboam and-all that he-did — are-they not written in-the-Book-of the-Chronicles-of the-Kings-of Judah?

**30** And-war was between Rehoboam and-Jeroboam all the-days.

**31** And-Rehoboam lay-down with his-fathers and-was-buried with his-fathers in-the-City-of David. And-the-name-of his-mother was Naamah the-Ammonite. And-Abijam his-son reigned in-his-place.

---
## EMET Textual Notes

1. **14:9 — "cast-me behind your-back"**: An extraordinary anthropomorphism — God treated as an object discarded, thrown behind someone's back. The imagery conveys both contempt and finality.

2. **14:10 — "bond and-free"**: Hebrew ʿatzur ve-ʿazuv — a merism meaning "every last male." The phrase appears in judgment contexts to indicate total annihilation of male heirs.

3. **14:13 — "a-good thing toward YHWH"**: The child Abijah is the one member of Jeroboam's house in whom God finds anything redeemable. His death is mercy — he alone receives burial instead of disgrace.

4. **14:15 — "as-a-reed sways"**: Israel is compared to a reed buffeted by water — rootless, unstable, soon to be uprooted entirely. This prophesies the Assyrian exile of the northern kingdom.

5. **14:27 — "shields-of bronze"**: Solomon's gold shields replaced by bronze replicas under Rehoboam. The substitution is a visual parable of decline — from gold to bronze in one generation.

— EMET
